angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 268,749 km at 3.56 pc = 1.01 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 280.7068 +/- 0.0203 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 3.56 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.3863 +/- 0.0021 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 15A: radius in solar radii, 0.3863 +/- 0.0021, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112): 268,749 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.423 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 15A: mass 0.423 solar masses from the K-band mass-luminosity relation of Henry & McCarthy (1993), not a dynamical mass (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3567 +/- 11 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 15A: effective temperature in K, 3567 +/- 11, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 15A: effective temperature in K, 3567 +/- 11, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/groombridge-34-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.891, rounded to two decimals
